Other local taxes (admissions and amusement, other)
Sewer, solid waste and water (operating $4,484,707, enterprise $30,000,978)
Other public works (gas, electric, light and power) (enterprise)

sources.label: MD Department of Legislative Services, Local Government Finances in Maryland, FY 2024: statement of revenues and expenditures and debt
MD Department of Legislative Services, local finance reports (history)
U.S. Census Bureau 2025 population estimates
U.S. Census Bureau 2024 Gazetteer (map location)

notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2024, from the town's uniform financial report to the Department of Legislative Services, adjusted and reconciled to its audited financial statements. Not a budget.
Covers all of the town's funds: governmental operations, capital projects and enterprise funds such as water, sewer and electric utilities. Capital spending counts in the year it happens.
Schools, most police and many other services are provided by the county, not the town, so town budgets are small next to county ones.

Miscellaneous spending ($1,817,885: pension contributions, health insurance, workers' compensation, Social Security and judgments) is spread across departments in proportion to their size, as with benefits in other states. Debt service is left out of that spread.
Debt is total public debt at the end of FY 2024: bonds, notes, loans (including State loans) and capital leases, less sinking fund assets, for both governmental and enterprise funds.
Political money is not scored: candidates for municipal office file campaign reports with their municipality, and there is no statewide database of those filings.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.
